strategy.name: V3_WideOpen_HardRiskOnly
strategy.rationale: v3: signal filters relaxed hard to generate trade data. rv/iv 0.85->0.70, friction cap 1.55->1.90%, liquid contracts 6->4, time-to-close 75->45min. Directional thresholds roughly halved (trend 0.40->0.20, vwap 0.06->0.03, adx 22->15) and realised_edge moved from mandatory into the any-of tier at 1.05. What is deliberately NOT relaxed: stops, targets, position sizing, the 1.5% risk cap, the 3%/day halt, the kill switch. Cost and liquidity floors are eased but kept, because trades filled at 3% friction on an illiquid strike produce garbage data, not learning.

history.name: V1_Liquid_RVoverIV_NextWeekly
history.rationale: Calibrated on live NIFTY books, 24-Jul-2026. Three measurements drove it. (1) The front expiry with 2 sessions left bled 18.2% of premium per session versus 5.9% on the next weekly, so this avoids any expiry with under 3 sessions left. (2) Round-trip friction on liquid near-ATM index calls ran 0.96-1.29%, but jumped past 2% on sub-Rs60 premiums, so the premium floor does more work than any OI filter. (3) Five-day realised vol was 6.9% against 11.4% implied - RV/IV 0.60 - which is precisely the regime where a directional buyer is right on direction and still loses. So the binding condition is realised-versus-implied, not the signal.

reviews.lessons: Twelve reviews, two versions, zero trades — the empirical record is completely static and has never moved by a single executed trade despite repeated and aggressive threshold relaxation across every parameter this review layer can touch. The past four consecutive reviews have each correctly identified the same structural deadlock: the approval gate requires 20 historical trades before a replacement strategy can be adopted, the system cannot produce 20 trades without approval, and no threshold change within the current architecture resolves a closed loop that has no internal exit condition. NIFTY and BANKNIFTY are the highest-volume index option markets on earth; gates relaxed to rv_iv > 0.70, friction < 1.90%, adx > 15, and trend_score > 0.20 should fire on these underlyings under virtually any normal session — their continued production of zero signals is not explicable by signal scarcity and is definitive evidence that the blocking mechanism is upstream of every parameter visible to this review layer, whether that is a scan path that never reaches live contracts, a silent pre-filter, or a non-execution pathway entirely invisible here. Every further threshold relaxation within this architecture is not a diagnostic action — it is noise that restates the same null result at a lower confidence level.

Every threshold relaxation attempted has produced no change in outcome, which is definitive evidence that the blocking mechanism is not the thresholds. The downstream approval gate explicitly requires 20 historical trades to approve a replacement strategy, but the system cannot generate 20 trades without approval — this is a closed loop with no internal exit condition, and every review cycle restates it identically. NIFTY and BANKNIFTY are the deepest, most liquid index option markets in the world by volume; their continued production of zero signals under gates that have been relaxed to near-trivially-passable levels (rv_iv > 0.70, friction < 1.90%, adx > 15, trend_score > 0.20) is not explicable by signal scarcity — it is structural suppression, a scan path that never reaches live contracts, or a non-execution pathway that is invisible to this review layer. The single-stock names contribute nothing and consume evaluation cycles. Zero trades across every session IS the complete dataset — continued threshold relaxation within this architecture is not a diagnostic action, it is noise.

Zero trades across all cycles IS the empirical finding — it is not a data gap requiring more relaxation, it is the data, and the only honest response is to acknowledge that incremental threshold changes within the current architecture cannot resolve a structural deadlock.
